newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-British shares, pound down after Tory rout.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-British shares, pound down after Tory rout.

text.p: London shares opened slightly weaker and the pound fell against the dollar on Friday after the Labour party's emphatic win in Britain's general election, while shares elsewhere in Europe firmed despite overnight losses on Wall Street.
The bigger-than-expected election rout for Britain's Conservative party, which had held power for 18 years, put Labour in government with a majority of about 180 seats.

Yet the early loss in the share market was less than many dealers had feared, with some arguing that the poll result should have been discounted and that the decisive poll outcome should ultimately prove positive for British markets.
The FTSE 100 index of top stocks, which set a record close on the eve of the poll, was down just 11.7 points at 4,433.3 at 0830 GMT, defying overnight talk of an early 50-point drop.

"There's an argument that we've known Labour was going to get in for months," said a dealer at one major securities house, "and now they've got such a huge majority there's a degree of certainty so we could see the market go higher."
Utility shares, in line for Labour's planned "windfall" tax, were among the biggest early losers and interest-rate sensitive banks also fell, though elsewhere declines were limited to a few pence.
But even in water and electricity stocks, the decline was far from savage with United Utilities Plc for instance down just 14-1/2p at 654-1/2 and Thames Water Plc down 6p at 673-1/2.

An interest rate rise is expected next week at the first post-election monetary policy meeting between the new Labour chancellor and the Bank of England, which has been pressing for higher rates for some months.

Gilts also retreated in the wake of the poll, with the long gilt future down 11/32 at 110-7/16, though a decline in sterling -- which stood at 1.6080 to the dollar at 0830 gmt compared with 1.6253 late on Thursday -- proved positive for exporting stocks whose earnings have been squeezed by the pound's strength in recent months.

Sterling firmed against the dollar and mark overnight, but came under pressure by early European trade when dealers cited a column in the Times newspaper which said Britain's new government "must create conditions for an immediate fall in the pound" to avoid economic damage.
Share prices in Frankfurt and Paris were slightly higher in early trade however, though many investors were on an extended weekend holiday following Thursday's May Day holiday.

In Paris, the CAC-40 index opened 0.25 percent higher at 2,646.05 and at 0830 GMT it was 0.4 percent higher at 2,649.90. In Frankfurt, the DAX index of leading shares was up 0.5 percent at 3,454.8 points.

But traders across Europe were circumspect ahead of the crucial U.S. jobs report for April due at 1230 gmt, which will be scrutinised for signs that wage inflation will spur further U.S. interest rate rises.

The U.S. Federal Reserve central bank plays close attention to jobs figures in gauging inflation pressures. It has nudged rates higher once already this year to counter inflation and meets again to review policy on May 20.
The dollar, meanwhile, was little affected by the British election, moving in ranges of about half a pfennig and half a yen during the overnight session.

Analysts said the currency market's focus would remain on sterling's moves until the U.S. payrolls data , with the dollar expected to drift until then. The sheer size of Labour's majority would make international investors nervous about sterling because of perceptions that the ruling party might have a freer hand in carrying out radical policies, they said.

"The sheer size of the victory has taken some of the shine off the pound already and that could continue...but although it's coming off a bit, it's still going to remain pretty firm in the near term," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International here.
"Once the new Chancellor (finance minister) convinces the markets that his policies are not going to be radical, sterling should pick up a bit," Lyons said.
Regarding the dollar, analysts said a strong payrolls data was unlikely to give the currency much of a boost, adding thata weaker figures were to have more of an impact.
STOCKS PRICES AT 0830 CMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 11.7 at 4,433.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 10.13 at 2,649.59.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 16.73 points at 3,454.80.
CURRENCIES AT 0830 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7220 marks compared with 1.7182 marks late in Europe on Thursday. It was at 126.68 yen after 126.57 yen late on Thursday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $340.15 an ounce in early trade compared with Wednesday's close of $339.65 in London.
